alignment.note: The Vulgate transmits an entirely different verse at this location (Mark 9:32b), reading 'At illi ignorabant verbum: et timebant interrogare eum' ('But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask him'). The Greek and Peshitta both preserve Jesus's passion prediction ('The Son of Man is delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him, and after being killed he will rise on the third day'), which the Vulgate omits here, likely due to textual displacement or harmonization with a different manuscript tradition that places this material elsewhere in the pericope.

The Vulgate uniquely attests the disciples' response ('But they did not understand the saying: and they were afraid to ask him') at this verse location, material that appears in Greek and Peshitta manuscripts at Mark 9:32. This represents either a scribal transposition or reflects a distinct Latin textual tradition that conflates or reorders the passion prediction and the disciples' incomprehension into a single verse unit.
